home.aboutHeading: Decoding the vascular roots of stroke and dementia
aboutParagraphs: The Hinman Lab is a translational neuroscience laboratory exploring the molecular pathways behind the brain's two most common disorders. We work across scales — from single glial cells and the oligovascular niche to human blood biomarkers — to understand how cerebrovascular dysfunction injures white matter and drives cognitive decline.

Our discoveries span neurovascular signaling, remyelination after stroke, 3D models of intracranial atherosclerosis, and biomarkers that are reshaping how vascular contributions to dementia are measured in the clinic.
home.highlightsText: A selection of recent publications. See the full list on the publications page.
home.contactText: We welcome inquiries from prospective trainees, collaborators, and partners in vascular brain health. Reach out — we'd love to hear from you.

research.heroHeading: From single vessels to the whole brain
research.fundingText: Our work is made possible by the generous support of public and private funders.
research.commitmentText: Across every program, we are committed to equity in education, science, and medicine — training the next generation of physician-scientists and ensuring the benefits of discovery reach the communities most affected by stroke and dementia.

join.heroHeading: Build the future of vascular brain health
join.heroText: We are always looking for curious, driven people to join our team. We train scientists at every stage and are committed to equity in education, science, and medicine.
join.opportunitiesText: If any of the paths below sound like you, we'd love to hear from you.

roles.title: Graduate Students
roles.body: UCLA graduate students (NSIDP and affiliated programs) interested in rotations on neurovascular biology, white matter injury, or biomarker discovery are encouraged to reach out.

roles.title: Postdoctoral Fellows
roles.body: We welcome postdocs with backgrounds in neuroscience, vascular biology, bioinformatics, or bioengineering who want to bridge molecular discovery and clinical translation.

roles.title: Undergraduates
roles.body: Motivated UCLA undergraduates can gain hands-on research experience in wet-lab, computational, and clinical projects. We value curiosity and commitment over prior experience.

roles.title: Clinical & Research Staff
roles.body: Staff and clinical research associates interested in coordinating studies on vascular contributions to cognitive impairment and dementia are encouraged to apply.

join.applyText: Send a brief note about your background, interests, and what draws you to the lab, along with a CV. We review every inquiry.
